character_sheet: The Basilisk is a giant hostile serpent: a tall head with a snout, a hinged lower jaw and six brow spikes, two neck blocks, six body blocks and a four-piece tapering tail, laid out nose to tip (ModelBasilisk.createBodyLayer, ModelBasilisk.java:71-180). It has 200 HP, 24 attack and 15 armour (MobStats.BASILISK, createAttributes Basilisk.java:92-101), walks through villages and wanders (:74-85), and fights on a 1-in-5 tick re-scan (customServerAiStep :201-237): the scanned target is slowed (Slowness V for 100 ticks — the 'gaze', :227) whether or not it is in reach, and within six blocks plus half its width the attacking flag rises and a bite lands on nested dice (:214-220) — one bite in three poisons for 8 to 14 seconds by difficulty and every bite knocks back (doHurtTarget :157-185). Hits are refused for 30 ticks after each one (hurt :188-194) and it heals 1 on a 1-in-75 roll (:234-236). It spawns at night in the dark with clear air above and no other Basilisk within 20 blocks (checkSpawnRules :284-291) in dark forests, jungles and old-growth birch (the hostile_basilisk biome modifiers); a baby is drawn at half size (BasiliskRenderer.java:41-42). Read it as a serpent: the whole body is one travelling wave, and the head never turns.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.25 of the rig, half that for a baby (BasiliskRenderer.java:29, :41-42; shadow 0.5 x 1.25) on a 256x64 sheet (ModelBasilisk.java:180); 1.6 x 3.5 block hitbox (ModEntities.java:50-53). The body and tail are a chain the code positions block by block (design section 5: real parent-child bones in the converted rig) — key the joints, never the positions.

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.1 = 0.314 rad (18 deg) x the walking speed, no threshold; each block an eighth of a period (pi/4) behind the one before, from body block 1 to the tail tip, and each placed at the end of the one before (12, 11, 12, 12, 12, 12, 10, 10, 10 units along)
groups.plain: the six body blocks and four tail segments yaw in a travelling wave with the walking speed, each an eighth of a turn behind the last, so the body snakes; still when standing
groups.math: seg_k.yRot = cos(t * 1.3 * 0.3 - k * pi/4) * pi * 0.1 * amount (k = 0..9: body1..body6, tail1..tail4); seg_(k+1).x/z = seg_k.x/z + cos/sin(seg_k.yRot) x length_k
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.3 x wingspeed 0.3 = 0.39 rad/tick: the natural period is 2 pi / 0.39 = 16.1 ticks

groups.name: jaw
groups.amplitude: attacking: pi x 0.18 = 0.565 rad (32 deg) about −1.0; not attacking: still at −1.1
groups.plain: the lower jaw chomps while the attacking flag is set and hangs still otherwise
groups.phase: the synced DATA_ATTACKING byte (Basilisk.java:46, set at :216 within reach, cleared at :229) selects; note the phase is ageInTicks x 0.45 WITHOUT the wingspeed
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.45 (no wingspeed factor on this line): the natural period is 2 pi / 0.45 = 13.96 ticks

behaviour: One speed-scaled travelling wave at 0.39 rad/tick (a 16.1-tick period) runs from the first body block to the tail tip: each of the ten segments yaws 18 degrees at top speed, an eighth of a period behind the one before, and is placed at the end of the previous segment (ModelBasilisk.java:186-213). Standing still the body is straight.

The lower jaw chomps 32 degrees at 0.45 rad/tick about −1.0 while the synced DATA_ATTACKING byte is set (Basilisk.java:46, raised at :216 within six blocks plus half the target's width) and hangs shut at −1.1 otherwise (ModelBasilisk.java:214).
The head, snout, brow spikes and the two neck blocks are static: the code never turns the head with the look, and the walk position plays no part.
The bite (doHurtTarget, Basilisk.java:157-185) and the Slowness 'gaze' (:227) are rolled by the 1-in-5 scan — nothing in the code fires an animation for them.

in `aggro_idle`: the jaw chomp the attacking branch shows (:214) plus a raised, fixed stare — the Slowness 'gaze' (Basilisk.java:227) deserves one
